title: Firewalls with iptables
summary: Turn an open router into a default-deny firewall that lets through only what the policy allows.

nodes.guest: a visitor's laptop on the same LAN, 10.16.1.66

tasks.title: Read the current policy
tasks.text: On the **router**, list the rules of the `FORWARD` chain (the chain for traffic passing *through* the router). What is its default policy?
hints: `iptables -L FORWARD -n -v` or `iptables -S FORWARD`. The policy is printed next to the chain name.

solution.note: `iptables -S FORWARD` prints `-P FORWARD ACCEPT`: anything is forwarded, so the router protects nothing.

tasks.title: Default deny, web allowed
tasks.text: Make the router drop forwarded traffic by default, but let replies to allowed connections back and let anyone on the LAN reach the **web server** (`10.16.2.10` TCP 80). The database (5432) must become unreachable.

checks.fail_msg: The FORWARD policy is not DROP yet.
admin can no longer load the web site.
guest can no longer load the web site.
The database port 5432 is still reachable from the LAN.

hints: Order: allow return traffic first, then the specific allow rule, then set the policy. `-A` appends a rule, `-P` sets the policy.
Return traffic: `iptables -A FORWARD -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT`.
Web: `iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.16.1.0/24 -d 10.16.2.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT`, then `iptables -P FORWARD DROP`.

steps.cmd: iptables -A FORWARD -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT && iptables -A FORWARD -s 10.16.1.0/24 -d 10.16.2.10 -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT && iptables -P FORWARD DROP

tasks.title: SSH for the admin only
tasks.text: The server's SSH port (22) must be reachable from **admin** (`10.16.1.10`) and from no one else. The guest must still get the web site.

checks.fail_msg: guest lost access to the web site.

hints: Match on the source address with `-s`. A single address needs no prefix.

tasks.title: The DMZ cannot reach in
tasks.text: If the DMZ server is ever compromised, it must not be able to open connections into the LAN. Make sure **server** cannot connect to the admin's file share at `10.16.1.10` port 9000, while the admin can still browse the web site.

checks.fail_msg: server can still open a connection to 10.16.1.10:9000.
admin lost access to the web site.

hints: If you built t2 correctly, this may already hold. Test it from the server.
Return traffic is allowed by the ESTABLISHED,RELATED rule, but a *new* connection from the DMZ matches no allow rule, so the DROP policy catches it.

solution.note: With a default-deny policy and only LAN-to-DMZ allow rules, a new connection from the DMZ is dropped. Nothing extra is needed. This is why default deny is the safe starting point.
